title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a fragment of Grothendieck's 1965 'Galois theory of motives' notes. The neighbouring pages are an unrelated Bourbaki-style draft on analytic ODEs.

The setting is motives over a finite field F_p. One considers pairs (C,α): C is a category of 'motives' (a Tannakian-type tensor category, perhaps attached to a torus or group T, written (C,T)), and α is extra structure at the fibre p, apparently tied to a choice of Frobenius or of an algebraic closure F̄_p. The deleted lines replace 'canonically equivalent' by 'equivalent up to isomorphism'.

The claims, in modern language:
(i) Two such pairs are equivalent, and the equivalences (C,α)→(C',α') form a connected groupoid. Any two equivalences φ,φ' are isomorphic, by an isomorphism unique up to a controlled ambiguity. The '[?] Z/nZ' is probably Ẑ, μ, or an automorphism group.
(ii) To each (C,α) one attaches a gerbe G(C,α) for the fpqc topology over A = ∏_ℓ Z_ℓ. The product explicitly includes ℓ = p and ℓ = ∞, i.e. an adelic object combining ℓ-adic, crystalline (p) and archimedean/Betti (∞) realizations. G(C,α) is the gerbe of fibre functors (equivalences) from C to the standard gerbe 'of type CC(A,T)', required at the fibre p to be compatible with α.
(iii) This gerbe is determined up to an equivalence unique up to a sign, independently of the choice of (C,α). But it depends on a choice of F̄_p, exactly as α does, because Gal(F̄_p/F_p) = Ẑ acts.
(iv) To remove this dependence, Grothendieck proposes defining F_{p^2}, or all of F̄_p, canonically via cyclotomic polynomials: F_{p^n} = F_p[T]/Φ_{p^n−1}(T), and F̄_p as the direct limit of these.

This anticipates the motivic Galois gerbe over F_p with realizations at all places, later made precise as the Langlands–Rapoport pseudomotivic groupoid and in Milne's work on motives over finite fields. It also anticipates the issue of canonical models of F̄_p.
errors: F_p[T]/Φ_{p^n−1}(T) is in general NOT a field. Over F_p, Φ_{p^n−1} splits into φ(p^n−1)/n distinct irreducible factors of degree n, so the quotient is a product of copies of F_{p^n}. It is a field only when φ(p^n−1) = n (e.g. p=2,n=2; p=3,n=1). A canonical choice therefore still requires selecting compatible irreducible factors. That is exactly the role later played by Conway polynomials, which are lexicographic and non-intrinsic. No truly intrinsic choice is possible, since Ẑ acts transitively on the compatible systems.
The connectedness/uniqueness claim for the groupoid of equivalences is stated with an unclear group ('Z/nZ'?) and 'à un signe près'. The precise ambiguity is not justified on the page.
CC(A,T) and the structure α are not defined on this page, so the gerbe construction cannot be fully checked.

ideas.what: Motivic Galois gerbe over F_p of fibre functors with values over ∏_ℓ Z_ℓ including ℓ=p (crystalline) and ℓ=∞, in the fpqc topology
ideas.modern_name: Motivic/pseudomotivic Galois gerbe over F_p; adelic realization gerbe (Langlands–Rapoport)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Tannakian/motivic Galois group idea), Saavedra Rivano (1972), Langlands–Rapoport (1987), Milne (1994)
ideas.where_published: Idea of motivic Galois group in letters to Serre and in Récoltes et Semailles; this specific adelic gerbe over ∏Z_ℓ not published by him

ideas.what: Gerbe determined up to equivalence unique up to sign, but depending on the choice of F̄_p (Ẑ-ambiguity)
ideas.modern_name: Dependence of the Weil-number/motivic gerbe on the choice of algebraic closure; band/lien ambiguity

ideas.what: Canonical construction of F_{p^n} and F̄_p via cyclotomic polynomials Φ_{p^n−1}
ideas.modern_name: Canonical/standard models of finite fields; Conway polynomials
ideas.usually_credited_to: Conway (c.1980s), Parker; Lenstra on canonical models

missed.claim: As early as 1965, Grothendieck considers an fpqc gerbe over ∏_ℓ Z_ℓ, including p and ∞, attached to motives over F_p. He notes that it is unique up to sign but depends on the choice of F̄_p. This prefigures the Langlands–Rapoport pseudomotivic gerbe and Milne's analysis of its dependence on choices.
missed.quote: il lui est associé une gerbe sur A=∏ Z_ℓ (ℓ y compris ℓ=p, ℓ=∞) ... mais elle dépend des choix d'un F̄_p — tout comme la structure α elle-même!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority for the adelic motivic gerbe over finite fields. It is relevant to current work on the Langlands–Rapoport conjecture and on the choice-dependence of motivic gerbes.

missed.claim: He attempts to rigidify F̄_p canonically via cyclotomic polynomials to remove the Ẑ-ambiguity. The proposal is flawed (the quotients are not fields), and the thread is left with '----'.
missed.quote: On peut s'en tirer en définissant canoniquement un F_{p^2} (ou = un F̄_p ...) par les polynômes cyclotomiques Φ_{p^n−1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It anticipates the Conway-polynomial approach, and shows that he saw rigidifying F̄_p as needed for a canonical motivic gerbe.

deep.surprise_reason: An early (1965) sketch of an adelic motivic gerbe over F_p, with explicit awareness of its dependence on F̄_p, which is not documented in Grothendieck's published texts. However, it is fragmentary, the notation is undefined, and the canonical-closure idea is erroneous. The broad ideas were later developed independently.
transcription_corrections: 'en fin [?] fpq [?]' is likely 'pour la top. fpqc' (fpqc topology).
'Z = Gal(F̄_p/F_p)' in the struck line is likely Ẑ = Gal(F̄_p/F_p).
'Z/nZ' in line 6 is uncertain; it could be Ẑ or an automorphism group. The reading is doubtful.
'type de CC(A,T)' probably refers to a standard gerbe/category of type C(A,T). Uncertain.
